scenario: Two passport-printing centres, Centre P and Centre Q, are evaluated on on-time delivery rates across urgent and routine applications. Centre P processes mainly urgent applications; Centre Q handles mostly routine ones.

data.description: On-time delivery rates by application urgency tier

question: (a) Which centre has the higher aggregate on-time rate? (b) Which performs better within each urgency tier? (c) Compute corrected rates using equal 50/50 tier weights.

ground_truth.explanation: Centre Q's inflated aggregate is driven by handling mainly routine (easier) applications. Within each tier, Centre P consistently outperforms Centre Q.

naive_answer: Centre Q is better; its aggregate on-time rate 0.935 exceeds Centre P's 0.8912.
naive_trap: Application urgency confounds the comparison: urgent applications are harder and Centre P handles seven times as many of them.
reasoning_trace: Urgent: P 0.88 > Q 0.83. Routine: P 0.97 > Q 0.95. P's aggregate is dragged down by its heavy urgent workload. Corrected 50/50: P=0.925, Q=0.89. P wins.
python_verification:
nPu,rPu,nPr,rPr = 700,0.88,100,0.97
nQu,rQu,nQr,rQr = 100,0.83,700,0.95
ovP=(nPu*rPu+nPr*rPr)/(nPu+nPr); ovQ=(nQu*rQu+nQr*rQr)/(nQu+nQr)
assert ovQ > ovP
cP=0.5*rPu+0.5*rPr; cQ=0.5*rQu+0.5*rQr
assert abs(cP-0.925)<0.005 and abs(cQ-0.89)<0.005
assert cP > cQ
